instructions:
# How to translate this chunk

This file holds `items`, a list of `{"k", "ctx", "t"}`. `t` is English text
that a reader of an Indian app or website sees. `ctx` is the field it came
from, such as label, hint, button, documents, brief or title. Use it to judge
tone and length: a label stays short, a hint can be a sentence.

Write `{"items": [{"k": ..., "t": ...}, ...]}` to the path in `write_to`.
Keep every `k` unchanged and in the same order. Put the translation in `t`.
Leave out `ctx`. Do not add, merge, split or drop items.

## Keep these exactly as they are

- Placeholders and markup: `{0}`, `{name}`, `%s`, `%d`, `%1$s`, HTML tags, `\n`.
- Website addresses, e-mail addresses and links.
- Every number: phone and toll-free numbers, Aadhaar, account, IFSC, PAN, PIN
  codes, amounts, dates, percentages. Write digits as 0-9, the Western digits,
  in every language, including Urdu. People type these into forms that take
  Western digits.
- Acronyms people know in Latin letters: OTP, PAN, IFSC, UPI, KYC, e-KYC, DBT,
  BPL, APL, NFSA, PM-KISAN, SMS, PDF, ID.

## Names

- Product, app, portal and scheme names: transliterate them into the script so
  they read naturally. Keep any acronym inside them in Latin, so "APPSC
  portal" becomes APPSC followed by the word for portal.
- A button or menu label quoted from a website, such as 'Apply Online' or
  'Register', stays in English inside quotes. The reader has to find that exact
  English word on the screen.
- People and places in examples are transliterated, never replaced with other
  names.
- Government office titles are transliterated so the reader can say them at
  the counter: Tahsildar, Patwari, Talathi, Mamlatdar, BDO, Collector, Gram
  Panchayat. The language notes below give the usual local forms.

## Tone

Write for an ordinary person who may be elderly and may have had little
schooling. Use everyday spoken language, not heavy official vocabulary. Where
people really say the English word, write it in the script: online, form,
portal, login, mobile, bank, certificate, download, upload, app. Keep
instructions short and direct, in the form "do this".

"Gender" means sex (male or female). It is never the word for caste.

## Before you write

Check that you have the same number of items as the input and that every
number and placeholder came through. Write the whole file in ONE Write call,
as valid UTF-8 JSON with no `\u` escapes and nothing else in the file.

## Hindi (hi)

Script: Devanagari. Used in UP, MP, Bihar, Rajasthan, Haryana, HP, Uttarakhand,
Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh and Delhi, and understood across the north.
Tone: everyday spoken Hindi (Hindustani). Avoid Sanskritised official words.
Words: ऑनलाइन, फॉर्म, पोर्टल, लॉगिन, आधार, बैंक, मोबाइल, OTP, हेल्पलाइन,
सर्टिफिकेट, डाउनलोड, अपलोड.
UI: आवेदन करें (Apply), जमा करें (Submit), आगे (Next), पीछे (Back), खोजें (Search),
शेयर करें (Share), सेटिंग (Settings), भाषा (Language), मदद (Help).
Offices: तहसीलदार, पटवारी, ग्राम पंचायत, कलेक्टर, ब्लॉक विकास कार्यालय (BDO).
Gender: लिंग (never जाति). Money: रु. 6,000; रु. 8 लाख. September: सितंबर.

## Gujarati (gu)

Script: Gujarati. Used in Gujarat, and spoken in Dadra & Nagar Haveli and
Daman & Diu.
Tone: everyday spoken Gujarati.
Words: ઓનલાઇન, ફોર્મ, પોર્ટલ, લૉગિન, આધાર, બેંક, મોબાઇલ, OTP, હેલ્પલાઇન, સર્ટિફિકેટ / દાખલો,
ડાઉનલોડ, અપલોડ.
UI: અરજી કરો, સબમિટ કરો, આગળ, પાછળ, શોધો, શેર કરો, સેટિંગ્સ, ભાષા, મદદ.
Offices: મામલતદાર, તલાટી, ગ્રામ પંચાયત, કલેક્ટર, તાલુકા પંચાયત.
Gender: જાતિ is caste; use લિંગ. Money: રૂ. 6,000; રૂ. 8 લાખ. September: સપ્ટેમ્બર.

## Marathi (mr)

Script: Devanagari. Used in Maharashtra, and widely in Goa.
Tone: everyday Marathi as spoken in Maharashtra.
Words: ऑनलाइन, फॉर्म, पोर्टल, लॉगिन, आधार, बँक, मोबाइल, OTP, हेल्पलाइन, दाखला / सर्टिफिकेट,
डाउनलोड, अपलोड.
UI: अर्ज करा, सबमिट करा, पुढे, मागे, शोधा, शेअर करा, सेटिंग्ज, भाषा, मदत.
Offices: तहसीलदार, तलाठी, ग्रामपंचायत, जिल्हाधिकारी (कलेक्टर), आपले सरकार सेवा केंद्र.
Gender: लिंग. Money: रु. 6,000; रु. 8 लाख. September: सप्टेंबर.

## Bengali (bn)

Script: Bengali. Used in West Bengal and Tripura, and in Assam's Barak Valley
and the Andamans.
Tone: everyday spoken Bengali (চলিত ভাষা), not সাধু ভাষা.
Words: অনলাইন, ফর্ম, পোর্টাল, লগইন, আধার, ব্যাংক, মোবাইল, OTP, হেল্পলাইন, সার্টিফিকেট,
ডাউনলোড, আপলোড.
UI: আবেদন করুন, জমা দিন, পরবর্তী, পিছনে, খুঁজুন, শেয়ার করুন, সেটিংস, ভাষা, সাহায্য.
Offices: বিডিও অফিস, গ্রাম পঞ্চায়েত, তহসিলদার, জেলাশাসক (কালেক্টর), দুয়ারে সরকার.
Gender: লিঙ্গ. Money: 6,000 টাকা; 8 লাখ টাকা. September: সেপ্টেম্বর.

## Assamese (as)

Script: Bengali script with the Assamese letters ৰ and ৱ. Used in Assam.
This is Assamese, not Bengali. Use Assamese words and spellings: আঁচনি
(scheme), বেংক (bank), কৰক (do), নহয় (is not).
Words: অনলাইন, প্ৰপত্ৰ / ফৰ্ম, পৰ্টেল, লগইন, আধাৰ, বেংক, মবাইল, OTP, হেল্পলাইন, প্ৰমাণপত্ৰ,
ডাউনল'ড, আপল'ড.
UI: আবেদন কৰক, দাখিল কৰক, পৰৱৰ্তী, উভতি যাওক, বিচাৰক, শ্বেয়াৰ কৰক, ছেটিংছ, ভাষা, সহায়.
Offices: চক্ৰ বিষয়াৰ কাৰ্যালয় (Circle Office), গাঁও পঞ্চায়ত, উন্নয়ন খণ্ড কাৰ্যালয় (BDO),
জিলা উপায়ুক্ত.
Gender: লিংগ. Money: 6,000 টকা; 8 লাখ টকা. September: ছেপ্তেম্বৰ.

## Punjabi (pa)

Script: Gurmukhi. Used in Punjab and Chandigarh, and spoken in Delhi and
Haryana.
Tone: everyday spoken Punjabi.
Words: ਆਨਲਾਈਨ, ਫਾਰਮ, ਪੋਰਟਲ, ਲੌਗਇਨ, ਆਧਾਰ, ਬੈਂਕ, ਮੋਬਾਈਲ, OTP, ਹੈਲਪਲਾਈਨ, ਸਰਟੀਫਿਕੇਟ,
ਡਾਊਨਲੋਡ, ਅਪਲੋਡ.
UI: ਅਰਜ਼ੀ ਦਿਓ, ਜਮ੍ਹਾਂ ਕਰੋ, ਅੱਗੇ, ਪਿੱਛੇ, ਖੋਜੋ, ਸਾਂਝਾ ਕਰੋ, ਸੈਟਿੰਗਾਂ, ਭਾਸ਼ਾ, ਮਦਦ.
Offices: ਤਹਿਸੀਲਦਾਰ, ਪਟਵਾਰੀ, ਸੇਵਾ ਕੇਂਦਰ, ਗ੍ਰਾਮ ਪੰਚਾਇਤ, ਡਿਪਟੀ ਕਮਿਸ਼ਨਰ.
Gender: ਲਿੰਗ. Money: ₹6,000; ₹8 ਲੱਖ. September: ਸਤੰਬਰ.

## Odia (or)

Script: Odia. Used in Odisha.
Tone: everyday spoken Odia.
Words: ଅନଲାଇନ, ଫର୍ମ, ପୋର୍ଟାଲ, ଲଗଇନ, ଆଧାର, ବ୍ୟାଙ୍କ, ମୋବାଇଲ, OTP, ହେଲ୍ପଲାଇନ, ସାର୍ଟିଫିକେଟ,
ଡାଉନଲୋଡ, ଅପଲୋଡ.
UI: ଆବେଦନ କରନ୍ତୁ, ଦାଖଲ କରନ୍ତୁ, ପରବର୍ତ୍ତୀ, ପଛକୁ, ଖୋଜନ୍ତୁ, ସେୟାର କରନ୍ତୁ, ସେଟିଂସ୍, ଭାଷା, ସାହାଯ୍ୟ.
Offices: ତହସିଲଦାର, ବିଡିଓ, ଗ୍ରାମ ପଞ୍ଚାୟତ, ଜିଲ୍ଲାପାଳ (କଲେକ୍ଟର), ମୋ ସେବା କେନ୍ଦ୍ର.
Gender: ଲିଙ୍ଗ. Money: ଟ.6,000; ଟ.8 ଲକ୍ଷ. September: ସେପ୍ଟେମ୍ବର.

Old Age Pension Scheme (Budhapa Pension)
Department of Social Security and Women & Child Development, Punjab

A pension of Rs 1,500 every month for women aged 58 and above and men aged 65 and above in Punjab whose income is low. The money is paid into the pensioner's bank account. You can apply online on Connect Punjab, at any Sewa Kendra, or by calling 1076 for an operator to come home. There is no fee and no paper form.
Rs 1,500 a month, paid into your bank account
Women aged 58 or above, men aged 65 or above
Total yearly income not more than Rs 60,000, counting business, rent and interest
Husband and wife together may own up to 2.5 acres of canal or well-irrigated (nehri/chahi) land, or up to 5 acres of barani or waterlogged land
You must be a resident of Punjab
The CDPO verifies the case within a month and the District Social Security Officer sanctions it
Aadhaar card (proof of identity, address and age)
A second proof of age: voter card or voter list entry, birth certificate or matriculation certificate
First page of the bank passbook
Village: land report from the Patwari. City: property verification from the Executive Officer of the Municipal Council
The elderly person who will get the pension, as written on Aadhaar.
As written on your Aadhaar or voter card.
Women can apply from 58, men from 65.
Must match the Aadhaar and your second age proof, such as the voter list or matric certificate.
Aadhaar e-KYC is done for this service, so give the pensioner's own number.
OTP and messages about the pension come here. A son's or daughter's number is fine.
Village Rampura Kalan, Tehsil Malout, Sri Muktsar Sahib
Where you live now. The CDPO of this area verifies the case.
Include rent, business and bank interest. The limit is Rs 60,000 a year.
Up to 2.5 acres nehri/chahi or 5 acres barani is allowed. The Patwari's report must say the same.
The pensioner's own account. Upload the first page of this passbook.
Open connect.punjab.gov.in, find Old Age Pension Scheme in the services list and tap Click to apply service. If you cannot go online, call 1076 and an operator will come home, or visit a Sewa Kendra.
Log in or register with your mobile number and OTP, and complete Aadhaar e-KYC for the person applying.
Fill in the form, upload the age proof, passbook page, self-declaration and the land or property report, and submit. There is no fee.
Note the application number on the receipt and follow it under Track on Connect Punjab.
The CDPO verifies your details and the District Social Security Officer sanctions the pension. The service time is 32 days online and 34 days at a Sewa Kendra.
After sanction, Rs 1,500 a month is credited to your bank account. For problems, contact the District Social Security Officer.
1100 (Connect Punjab and Sewa Kendra helpline) / 1076 (doorstep service) / 0172-2608746 (Social Security head office) / 14567 (elderly helpline)
Lado Protsahan Yojana (Lado Sankalp Patra)
Directorate of Women Empowerment, Women & Child Development Department, Government of Rajasthan

A girl born in a government hospital or a JSY-approved private hospital in Rajasthan is promised Rs 1.5 lakh, paid in seven instalments from birth until she graduates at 21. The scheme began on 1 August 2024, replaced the old Mukhyamantri Rajshri Yojana (Rajshri girls get their remaining instalments under Lado), and was raised from Rs 1 lakh to Rs 1.5 lakh in 2025. There is no form: the hospital, the school and the college record her details, and every instalment goes by DBT.
Rs 1,50,000 in 7 instalments — Rs 2,500 at birth up to Rs 1 lakh at graduation
The mother is a resident of Rajasthan and has an Aadhaar card and a Jan Aadhaar card
The girl is born in a government hospital or in a private hospital approved under Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY)
The guidelines set no income or caste condition, and no limit on the number of children for the 3rd instalment onwards
Instalments 3 to 6 need admission in a government school or a state-recognised private school
The last instalment needs graduation from a recognised institution and age 21 completed
A mother living in Rajasthan who delivered outside the state and got JSY can claim the first instalment at her local government hospital
Jan Aadhaar card of the family; add the girl's name after birth
Bank passbook of the mother (father or guardian if the mother has died)
Pregnancy (ANC) registration done with the ANM or government hospital
Mamta card showing all vaccinations done by 9–12 months, for the 2nd instalment
School admission entry on Shala Darpan or the private school portal, for instalments 3 to 6

No form and no fee. During pregnancy, register at the ANC check-up with the ANM, ASHA or government hospital and give the mother's Aadhaar, Jan Aadhaar and bank details for the PCTS entry. Deliver in a government hospital or a JSY-approved private hospital. School instalments come through the school's Shala Darpan entry and the last one through the college. For a missing instalment, ask the ANM or the Block Chief Medical Officer for the first two, the school head for instalments 3 to 6, or the district Women Empowerment office.
Exactly as on the Aadhaar and the bank account, or the payment can bounce.
The ANM enters this at the first pregnancy check-up.
The family's 10-digit Jan Aadhaar. If the family has none, get it made at e-Mitra before the delivery.
An account in the mother's own name. The first six instalments go to the parent; the last one goes to the girl.
Register early in pregnancy with the ANM; this PCTS entry is what starts the scheme.
Only a government hospital or a JSY-approved private hospital counts. A home birth is not covered.
Given at birth. Quote it for every instalment and at school admission.
All vaccines due by 9–12 months. The second Rs 2,500 is paid once this shows on PCTS.
Govt. Senior Secondary School, Bilara — Class 1
The school enters her on Shala Darpan at Class 1, 6, 10 and 12, using her PCTS ID, Jan Aadhaar or APAAR ID.
Register the pregnancy at the first check-up with the ANM, ASHA or government hospital, and give the mother's Aadhaar, Jan Aadhaar, bank account and mobile number.
Deliver in a government hospital or a JSY-approved private hospital. The girl gets a PCTS ID and the family gets the Rs 1.5 lakh Sankalp Patra.
The first Rs 2,500 is credited to the mother's account after the hospital birth, without any application.
Complete all vaccinations by 9–12 months on the Mamta card. When PCTS is updated, the second Rs 2,500 is paid; no proof that the child is alive is asked.
Add the girl to the Jan Aadhaar. On admission to Class 1, 6, 10 and 12 the school records her, and the Education Department pays Rs 4,000, Rs 5,000, Rs 11,000 and Rs 25,000.
After she passes graduation and turns 21, Rs 1 lakh goes to her own account. Missing one stage does not stop the later instalments.
If a payment does not arrive, ask the ANM or the school to check the entry, or complain on 181.
181 — Rajasthan Sampark (state helpline for complaints about any scheme)
Directorate of Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS), Women & Child Development Department, Government of Rajasthan

Gives Rs 6,000 in three instalments to a woman pregnant with her second child, for better food and care. It was earlier called the Indira Gandhi Matritva Poshan Yojana; only the name changed and the rules are the same. If the second baby is a boy, the third instalment is Rs 4,000; if it is a girl, she gets Rs 6,000 under the central PM Matru Vandana Yojana instead, making Rs 8,000 in all. There is no form: the Anganwadi worker or ANM records the pregnancy on PCTS and the money comes by DBT.
Rs 6,000 in 3 instalments for the second child (Rs 8,000 in all if it is a girl)
Woman pregnant with her second child on or after 1 April 2022 (1 November 2020 in Pratapgarh, Dungarpur, Banswara, Udaipur and Baran)
Runs in all districts; pregnant or breastfeeding Anganwadi workers, helpers, ASHA sahyoginis and saathins are also eligible
Not for women regularly employed by the Centre, the state or a PSU, or getting the same kind of benefit under another law
Not eligible if the first pregnancy gave twins, or if after remarriage either partner already has more than one child
Cannot take MMMPY and PM Matru Vandana instalments for the same conditions
After a miscarriage or still birth, she stays eligible in a later pregnancy
Jan Aadhaar card (it will be made at registration if the family has none)
Mamta card (mother and child protection card) — photocopy
Bank passbook copy of the account linked to the Jan Aadhaar

No form and no fee. Register the pregnancy at the Anganwadi centre, or with the ANM at the sub-centre or government hospital, within 120 days of the last period. Give the Jan Aadhaar, Mamta card, bank passbook and mobile number for the PCTS entry; the instalments then come on their own as the check-ups and the hospital delivery are recorded. For a missing instalment, ask the Anganwadi worker or the CDPO (ICDS project office) of your block.
As on the Jan Aadhaar and the bank account.

The first instalment needs registration within 120 days of this date.
Second pregnancy — 1 living child (son, 4 years)
MMMPY is for the second child only. The first child is covered under PM Matru Vandana Yojana.
Register as early as you can; this PCTS entry is your application.
Every check-up and vaccine is written on this card. Keep it safe.
Your own account linked to the Jan Aadhaar. The money is paid only by DBT.
The third instalment needs a hospital delivery.
As soon as you know you are pregnant, and within 120 days of the last period, go to the Anganwadi worker or ANM and register. Give your Jan Aadhaar and mobile number.
Get your Mamta card. Your details go on PCTS; there is no form to fill.
First instalment: Rs 1,000 is paid after registration within 120 days.
Second instalment: Rs 1,000 after at least two check-ups within the first six months of pregnancy.
Deliver in a hospital. For a boy (or transgender child) the third instalment is Rs 4,000; for a girl, Rs 6,000 comes in one go under PM Matru Vandana Yojana instead.
The money goes to the account linked to your Jan Aadhaar, with an SMS. If an instalment is missing, ask the Anganwadi worker to check the PCTS entry, or call 181.
181 — Rajasthan Sampark; your Anganwadi worker or the block CDPO office for PCTS entries
Mukhyamantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (Rajasthan top-up to PM-Kisan)

Rajasthan adds its own money to PM-Kisan. Every Rajasthan farmer family that receives PM-Kisan also gets Rs 3,000 a year from the state, paid in instalments of Rs 1,000, so the total becomes Rs 9,000 a year with the Centre's Rs 6,000. There is no separate state form: a farmer registered and active in PM-Kisan gets the state money by DBT automatically.
Rs 3,000 a year from the state on top of PM-Kisan's Rs 6,000 (Rs 9,000 in all)
Rajasthan farmer family that is an active PM-Kisan beneficiary
Farm land in own name as on 1 February 2019; land got later only by inheritance counts
One person per family — husband, wife and minor children count as one family
Farmer ID from the Rajasthan Farmer Registry, PM-Kisan e-KYC done, and an Aadhaar-linked bank account open for DBT
PM-Kisan exclusions apply: income-tax payers, government employees, pensioners drawing Rs 10,000 or more a month, doctors, lawyers and other registered professionals
Aadhaar card, with a mobile number linked for OTP
Farmer ID (Rajasthan Farmer Registry), made free at e-Mitra, a CSC or a registry camp
Jamabandi (land record) copy showing the land in your name
Bank passbook of an Aadhaar-linked account open for DBT
The farmer's own 12-digit Aadhaar. The name on the land record must match it.
The OTP and every payment SMS come here.
Choose Rajasthan; only then is the state's Rs 3,000 added.
From the Rajasthan Farmer Registry. Get it at e-Mitra, a CSC or a camp if you do not have one.
Where the farm land is, not where you live now.

Copy them from your jamabandi. The patwari checks them against the land record.

Open New Farmer Registration on pmkisan.gov.in, enter Aadhaar and mobile, choose Rajasthan, verify the OTP, fill in the land and bank details and submit. Note the registration number. e-Mitra or a CSC can do this for you.
The patwari and the tehsil verify the land, and the state approves the record.
Finish e-KYC with an Aadhaar OTP, face authentication or a fingerprint at a CSC, and make sure the bank account is linked to Aadhaar.
Once active, PM-Kisan pays Rs 2,000 three times a year and the state pays its Rs 1,000 instalments separately, all by DBT.
Check payments on pmkisan.gov.in under Know Your Status, or on the Jan Soochna portal.
Nirman Shramik Panjiyan — BOCW Welfare Board (Shramik Card)
Rajasthan Building & Other Construction Workers Welfare Board, Labour Department, Government of Rajasthan

Registers a construction worker with the state welfare board and gives a beneficiary identity card, the shramik card. With it the worker and family can claim the board's schemes: Rs 55,000 under Shubhshakti for a woman worker or an adult unmarried daughter, Rs 21,000 maternity help for a girl and Rs 20,000 for a boy, scholarships for children, up to Rs 1.5 lakh towards a house, and Rs 5 lakh if the worker dies in an accident. Registration is online through SSO and the Labour Department's LDMS, by the worker or at an e-Mitra kiosk.
Shramik card for the board's schemes — Rs 55,000 Shubhshakti, Rs 20,000–21,000 maternity help, Rs 5 lakh accident cover

Log in at sso.rajasthan.gov.in (make a free SSO ID with Jan Aadhaar if needed) and open LDMS, or go to an e-Mitra kiosk.
In LDMS choose BOCW Welfare Board, then Beneficiary Registration, and fill in Form V: your details, address, employers of the last 12 months, family and nominee.
Upload the photo, age proof and worker certificate, choose your labour office, tick the declaration and submit. Save the application number.

The labour office checks the form. If it asks for a missing paper, upload it from the same login. When approved, it asks you to pay the Rs 25 registration fee and Rs 60 contribution online or at e-Mitra.
After payment, print your beneficiary identity card (shramik card) from Print Identity Card in LDMS.
